findings.passage: Last year there was an issue with an HOA, it wasn’t in the state, it was outside the state, that was banning guns. We did that proactively," Rohl said. "During that process it came to light that these covenants do exist West River dating back to the 1900s in a lot of cases. That’s why the original intent of the bill was actually to break those. We hit a roadblock with that on the House side, so we figured it’s at least better to at least stop them going forward.

Said the original aim was to break existing covenants, but the House blocked that, so the bill now covers new covenants only.
